entries.title: Add "general knowledge" category to the reflection roadmap
entries.summary: Extended the engineering-reflection skill with a cross-cutting "general knowledge" category — durable craft/workflow insight that isn't a bug or a trade-off — surfaced in its own topic-grouped panel plus a knowledge node type. Seeded it with the workflow lessons learned so far.
learnings: The roadmap now aggregates craft notes across the whole journey into one topic-grouped panel, so general knowledge is a running cheat-sheet separate from the per-milestone tree.

knowledge.insight: Compact constantly and keep an eye on window size; close a session once its context is no longer relevant instead of letting it bloat — stale context is a cost, not a safety net.
Split different problems across separate agents/sessions. Each session's window is scoped to one problem, so the right context gets sent every time instead of one giant window carrying everything.

CLI is best for straightforward commands but is prone to fat-fingering a long/complex invocation; MCP gives exact, structured usage for complex tasks (e.g. exposing data). Reach for CLI for simple ops, MCP when precision on a complex call matters.

entries.impact: The journey now captures how-to-work knowledge, not just what-got-built, so hard-won workflow lessons are remembered across projects.

entries.title: Grokking the injectable LLM port (ports & adapters)
entries.summary: Asked what "ports-and-adapters architecture (injectable LLM port)" actually means. Walked through SkillGuard's own port.py (the LLMJudge Protocol) and anthropic_judge.py (the concrete adapter) to see how the Detection Engine depends only on the interface, letting a real Claude adapter run in prod and a deterministic stub run in tests.
learnings: The Detection Engine never imports the Anthropic SDK — it talks only to the LLMJudge Protocol (a structural interface). AnthropicJudge is one adapter; a test stub is another.
"Injectable" means the engine receives an LLMJudge from outside rather than constructing one, so tests can pass a stub with hard-coded verdicts (no network, no API key, deterministic).
Python's Protocol gives structural typing: anything with a matching judge() method IS an LLMJudge, no inheritance required.
The pattern also quarantines the security-critical untrusted-data framing (ADR 0002) inside one adapter instead of smearing it across the codebase.

knowledge.insight: Keep core logic depending on an interface (port), never a concrete external system; plug real vs fake implementations in from outside (inject). The payoff is testability — swap a non-deterministic, costly dependency (an LLM, a DB, the network) for a controlled stub without touching the core.

entries.impact: Turned a named-but-fuzzy architecture term into a concrete mental model anchored in the project's own files, so future changes to the LLM layer are reasoned about at the right seam.

entries.title: Why two hooks: SessionStart barrier vs PreToolUse backstop
entries.summary: Worked through how Claude Code hooks fire and why SkillGuard needs two of them: SessionStart runs once at boot (before skill descriptions load) and can quarantine files, while PreToolUse fires before every Skill/Bash call to catch Skills that arrive mid-session.
learnings: SessionStart is a one-shot snapshot at launch (typing `claude`) and boot blocks until it returns — that blocking is what realises the 'hold on unknown' rule.
SessionStart is the ONLY hook that can protect a Skill's description surface, because descriptions load into context at boot before any tool call, so PreToolUse never gets a chance at them.
PreToolUse exists purely to cover SessionStart's blind spot: Skills that land after boot (agent-generated, downloaded, or git-cloned mid-session) since SessionStart already fired and won't re-run.
The 'SessionStart-before-load' ordering is a load-bearing assumption — if Claude Code ever loaded descriptions before running SessionStart, the barrier would regress to next-session-only.

knowledge.insight: Hooks are shell commands the harness runs at lifecycle points, not model choices — that's why they're reliable for enforcement. They take a JSON event on stdin and return JSON on stdout; PreToolUse is a veto point that can deny a tool call before it runs.
A hook subprocess is fed stdin on a pipe, so isatty() is false — a clean signal for 'no human present' to degrade interactive prompts to a safe non-blocking default instead of hanging.

entries.impact: Clarified the defense-in-depth rationale behind SkillGuard's two enforce points, making the boot-time vs use-time distinction concrete.

entries.title: Grilling the Control Plane: herd immunity + the fat-gate pivot
entries.summary: A grill-with-docs session that designed the next step — a Control Plane vertical slice where one machine scans and the whole fleet adopts the Verdict. Surfaced that the shipped code (local engine per gate) contradicts ADR 0001 (thin client, upload-on-miss), reconciled the record, and produced PRD 0003 + ADR 0004.

tradeoffs.chosen: Adopt all Verdict tiers from the Control Plane, Clean included (hash-bound + engine_version-gated)
tradeoffs.rejected: Asymmetric trust: adopt Malicious/Suspicious but always re-scan on Clean
tradeoffs.why: User pushed back — Clean is the common case, so re-scanning every Clean Skill on every machine throws away nearly all the compute savings. Safety comes from content-hash binding + engine-version gating, not from refusing Clean.

tradeoffs.chosen: Model 2 — fat gate with a local engine, sharing only Verdict metadata (content never leaves the machine)
tradeoffs.rejected: Model 1 — thin client that uploads Skill content on a miss for central scanning (ADR 0001 as written)
tradeoffs.why: The code already ships a local engine, so Model 2 matches reality, keeps the Control Plane lightweight (no server-side LLM), and gives a strong privacy line. Cost: the CP can't independently verify a pushed verdict (rogue-writer gap), deferred to future write-auth.

tradeoffs.chosen: React + Postgres for the Control Plane (industry-standard, resume-worthy)
tradeoffs.why: User wanted something show-off-worthy for a hiring manager. Scoped to avoid friction: React built and served as static from FastAPI (one process), Postgres only in the cloud CP while the endpoint store stays embedded.

learnings: The local Verdict Store is the CACHE; the Control Plane Postgres is the SOURCE OF TRUTH — opposite roles. The endpoint caches from the cloud origin, so Postgres is never the 'cache'.
Herd immunity = scan each unique Skill once per fleet, not once per machine. Adopting Clean verdicts is where the savings live, since most Skills are Clean.

What makes trusting a remote Verdict safe is content-hash binding (adopt only for exact bytes) + engine_version gating (adopt only if the remote engine >= mine) — not wall-clock freshness; a fresh wrong verdict is still wrong.

Verdict (deduped per content, no machine) and Sighting (per-machine encounter, with a Source of scanned/adopted/cache) are two different concepts — the dashboard needs the per-machine dimension a Verdict doesn't carry.

The CP query slots into evaluate() as a nullable ControlPlanePort mirroring the existing EnginePort/AllowlistPort; cp=None means standalone-local, which IS the fail-safe and keeps the existing test suite green.

knowledge.insight: Cross-check ADRs against the code as you design — a shipped decision can silently diverge from its ADR (here the engine went local while ADR 0001 still assumed a thin client). When you find the contradiction, reconcile the record (amend/supersede) rather than paper over it, or the next reader trusts a stale doc.

Endpoint-agent + central-server shape: keep a light agent on every endpoint and one heavy DB in the cloud (EDR/Sentry/Datadog pattern). Two stores with opposite roles — embedded cache on the endpoint, authoritative DB centrally. For a demo you collapse the whole topology (server + DB + several agents) onto one laptop, but say so when presenting.

Injecting an optional dependency as a NULLABLE port whose None-case is the safe fallback gives you the degrade-gracefully behavior for free and keeps every existing test passing untouched — the absence of the adapter is a first-class, safe mode.

entries.impact: Turned a vague 'what's next' into a fully-grilled, buildable Control Plane slice with the architecture pivot (fat gate, metadata-only) reconciled across ADR 0001/0004, PRD 0003, and the glossary.
